title: The Rule of 72: How Fast Your Money Doubles
hook_text: THE MATH THEY HIDE FROM YOU

beats.say: An 8% investment takes 9 years to double, but your 24% credit card debt only takes 3.
beats.visual: A split-screen style cinematic shot. On the left, a green bank ledger book lies closed on a dark oak desk. On the right, a stack of red bills with a heavy iron padlock resting on top. Moody, high-contrast lighting.

beats.say: Here's the hidden math keeping you trapped, and the simple, compounding formula you can use to escape.
beats.visual: Close-up of a person's hands holding an old brass compass over an open, blank leather journal on a wooden table. Warm, low-key lighting.

beats.say: It's called the Rule of 72, a powerful mental shortcut quietly used by wealthy wall street bankers.
beats.visual: A glass-walled conference room overlooking a dim city skyline at dusk. A polished dark mahogany table reflects the soft overhead lights.

beats.say: You simply divide 72 by your interest rate to find the exact years it takes.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a vintage analog stopwatch ticking. The silver metal casing gleams under a soft key light. Shallow depth of field.

beats.say: If you earn 8% a year, your money doubles every 9 years like clockwork.
beats.visual: A small, vibrant green seedling sprouting from rich dark soil inside a rustic clay pot on a sunlit window sill. Soft morning light.

beats.say: Your initial $10,000 investment becomes $20,000, then $40,000, and quietly grows completely on autopilot.
beats.visual: An overhead shot of neat stacks of crisp hundred-dollar bills sitting inside a dark velvet-lined drawer, lit by a single dramatic shaft of light.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions: this exact same math works against you twice as fast.
beats.visual: A dark, moody shot of a massive iron gear mechanism turning slowly inside an old clock tower, cast in deep shadows.

beats.say: The average credit card now charges a brutal 24% annual interest rate.
beats.visual: A close-up from behind of a hand holding a sleek, unbranded black credit card over a dark slate countertop. Cool blue tones.

beats.say: Divide 72 by 24, and your unpaid debt doubles every 3 years.
beats.visual: A close-up of dark storm clouds gathering rapidly over an empty asphalt highway at sunset. Moody, dramatic contrast.

beats.say: That small $3,000 emergency balance quickly becomes $6,000, then $12,000, trapping you in an endless cycle.
beats.visual: A vintage metal scale balancing, with one side heavily weighed down by a dark, rough iron block. Deep shadows, industrial look.

beats.say: While your retirement savings creep forward, your high-interest debt compounds at three times the speed.
beats.visual: A time-lapse style shot of dry autumn leaves swirling in a cold wind across a cracked concrete ground under a gray sky.

beats.say: If you're ready to master these numbers, follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A person's silhouette standing in front of a massive, glowing window looking out over a sprawling, modern city at night.

beats.say: It all starts by understanding why
beats.visual: A hand in shadow slowly turning a heavy brass key in an ancient, ornate keyhole. Close-up, cinematic atmosphere.

caption: The Rule of 72 is the most important math formula you will ever learn. Here is how it can build your wealth—or quietly destroy it.
description: This video breaks down the Rule of 72 using real numbers. It explains how an 8% investment takes 9 years to double, while 24% credit card debt doubles in just 3 years.
first_comment: What is the interest rate on your highest-interest account right now?

facts.claim: Rule of 72: at 8% money doubles every 9 years; at 24% debt doubles every 3 years
